description: Tier-1 self-authored Figma fixtures for the dashscene importer (see docs/decisions/figma-corpus-self-authored-only.md). Each entry maps a fixture name to the Figma file key of a file authored in the project's own account. The capture tooling fetches GET /files/:fileKey?plugin_data=shared (docs/decisions/figma-access-plan-and-pat-policy.md, docs/decisions/annotator-plugin-contract-frozen.md) and commits the returned JSON into corpus/figma-fixtures/<name>.json for offline record-and-replay (docs/design/dashc.md).
provenance: self-authored via the fixture-author dev plugin (importers/figma/plugin/fixture-author); Community-license-safe because nothing captured here is a third-party file (docs/decisions/figma-corpus-self-authored-only.md).

captureParams.note: ?plugin_data=shared is always passed so sharedPluginData roles (docs/decisions/annotator-plugin-contract-frozen.md) round-trip even though no fixture carries them yet.

fixtures.name: backdrop-blur
fixtures.covers: the BACKGROUND_BLUR construct for the v0.11 backdrop-blur story (docs/decisions/backdrop-blur-is-core-vocabulary.md): a 200x90 frosted panel (corner radius 16, white at 0.2 alpha, BACKGROUND_BLUR radius 16) over three hard-edged vertical bands and a circle, in a fixed 320x180 frame
fixtures.note: Authored with the fixture-author plugin's backdrop-blur command; fully scripted, so the file carries no _manual-checklist annotation (debt #382). Story #393 made backdrop blur core vocabulary that lowers into the schema, so the fixture emits with the frosted panel present and raises no diagnostic. Stage B-4 wired its oracle frame (goldens/oracle/import-manifest.json, frame backdrop-blur, node 1:2), which measures 10/57600 px (0.017%) against Figma's own render and is classified aa-edge from that residual — every differing pixel is the ELLIPSE's anti-aliased edge, while the blurred region itself stays within a max delta of 16.

fixtures.name: vector-backdrop-blur
fixtures.covers: the BACKGROUND_BLUR construct on a baked VECTOR (debt #413): a frosted ring (outer r=64, hole r=32, white at 0.2 alpha, BACKGROUND_BLUR radius 16) centred in the frame, over the same three hard-edged bands and circle as the backdrop-blur fixture, in a fixed 320x180 frame
fixtures.note: Authored with the fixture-author plugin's vector-backdrop-blur command and captured. Fully scripted, so the file carries no _manual-checklist annotation (debt #382). This is the baked-vector twin of the backdrop-blur fixture: the Skia painter renders a frosted FRAME through draw_backdrop_blur_box and a frosted VECTOR through draw_backdrop_blur_field, and only the second is the path the live hero's frosted panel takes. The backdrop is identical to backdrop-blur's by construction (both commands call blurBackdrop), so the two frames differ in exactly one thing and their residuals are directly comparable. What the ring measures is the coverage mask: the hole and the quad's four corners lie inside the bounding quad but outside the baked outline, so both must render as sharp backdrop, and a blur confined to the box frosts them. That is a different defect from the one PR #403 fixed, whose signature is outside the quad entirely. The ring is centred in the frame rather than on a seam because the corner regions are the larger uncovered area and centring puts both seams inside them: modelled numerically a box-confined blur measures about 4.1 percent centred against about 1.9 percent seam-centred, and the aa-edge budget is 2 percent. Its oracle frame is wired after capture, and its tolerance band is classified from the measured residual, never from expectation.
